\section{Calibrated simulation}\label{sup:v8-calibrated}

\subsection{Data-generating processes and calibration}\label{sup:v8-mc-calibration}

This experiment asks how the declared forecasting procedures behave under fixed calibrated laws. It adds simulated data only. Parameters use the original pre-validation prefix: 10463 FX observations ending 2015-10-07, and 329 Treasury observations ending 2019-07-17. Whole-file byte counts and hashes were verified before prefix estimation. Each source is divided by its prefix population standard deviation without centering; the intercept retains its level mean. Native scales, dates and identities remain in \texttt{calibration.json}.

For the Gaussian constant-variance control D0 and the conditional-volatility laws D1/D2, respectively,

\begin{align*}
\mathrm{D0}:\quad &N_t=c+\phi N_{t-1}+\sigma z_t,\qquad z_t\sim\mathcal N(0,1),\\
\mathrm{D1/D2}:\quad &N_t=c+\phi N_{t-1}+s_tu_t,\quad u_t=\sqrt{v_t}z_t,\\
&v_t=\omega+\alpha u_{t-1}^2+\beta v_{t-1},\quad z_t=\sqrt{(\nu-2)/\nu}\,T_t,\quad T_t\sim t_\nu.
\end{align*}

D0 and D2 share the Treasury-prefix AR fit; D1 uses the FX prefix. Least squares estimates the intercept and AR slope, with the fixed restriction $\phi\in[-0.995,0.995]$. A binding restriction would trigger the prespecified intercept reestimate, not a new slope search. The restriction did not bind for either source. D1 multiplies latent shocks by the known hour shape below; D0/D2 have unit shape. GARCH is fitted once to AR residuals, divided by the hour shape for D1. It uses zero-mean GARCH with standardized Student-t innovations and package defaults, \texttt{rescale=False}, and no restart. The executed \texttt{arch} version was 8.0.0; see the \href{https://arch.readthedocs.io/en/latest/univariate/introduction.html}{package model documentation} and \href{https://arch.readthedocs.io/en/latest/univariate/generated/arch.univariate.StudentsT.html}{standardized Student-t definition}.

For D1, let $r_t$ be an AR residual and $n_h$ its count at hour $h$. Set $a_h^2=\sum_{t:\,h(t)=h}r_t^2/n_h$ and $s_h=a_h/\sqrt{\sum_h n_ha_h^2/\sum_h n_h}$. Thus the observation-weighted mean squared shape is 1.0. A missing hour or nonpositive RMS would fail calibration. All fitted shapes are retained:

Initialize $N=c/(1-\phi)$, $u=0$ and $v=\omega/(1-\alpha-\beta)$; D0 instead uses $v=\sigma^2$. The fixed burn-in is 10000 or the larger of $\lceil 10/(1-|\phi|)\rceil$ and $\lceil 10/(1-\alpha-\beta)\rceil$, omitting the GARCH term for D0. Required burn-in above 1000000 fails calibration. Every archived fitted law used 10000 burn-in records. Nonconvergence, nonfinite or inadmissible GARCH parameters, or nonstationarity would fail the law; none was repaired. Calibration uncertainty is not propagated through the repetitions.

The hourly clock starts at 2000-01-03 00:00:00, with 120 hourly records followed by a 48-hour gap, including during burn-in. The weekly clock starts at 2000-01-05 00:00:00. Its spacing is weekly. The clocks are known to the oracle; the hourly convention idealizes holidays.

\subsection{Forecasts, information sets and execution}\label{sup:v8-mc-procedure}

The main grid has 24 cells: $W\in\{52,260,720,2880\}$ and $p\in\{4,33\}$ for each law. $H=6$ and $\tau=0.95$ are fixed. Predictor counts exclude the intercept. The smaller set contains current magnitude, signed current level, and short/long past-increment RMS. The larger set reuses the existing lagged levels, magnitude, RMS, calendar and gap construction; constant weekly calendar/gap columns are retained. No new forecast family or changed solver is introduced.

\begin{table}[htbp]\centering\scriptsize

\caption{Fixed zero-based origin geometry. Each law shares one generated path and oracle across all its history/predictor cells in a repetition. RMS entries are short/long past spans.}\label{tab:v8-mc-geometry}

\begin{tabular}{llrrrrr}\toprule
Law & Clock & Validation origins & Evaluation origins & $V$ & Refit & RMS spans\\\midrule
D0 & Weekly & 2911--2962 & 2969--3468 & 52 & 13 & 6/26 \\
D1 & Hourly & 3053--4492 & 4499--4998 & 1440 & 24 & 24/168 \\
D2 & Weekly & 2911--2962 & 2969--3468 & 52 & 13 & 6/26 \\
\bottomrule\end{tabular}\end{table}

With first valid feature origin $L$, validation starts at $a=L+W_{\max}+H-1$ and ends at $a+V-1$; evaluation starts at $b=a+V+H$ and ends at $b+M-1$. Generate through $b+M-1+H$. At refit $r$, the training origins are exactly $r-H-W+1,\ldots,r-H$; their peak labels have matured. Validation labels end before evaluation starts. Future labels never enter a fit early.

Historical $F$ uses headroom rank $\lceil\tau(W+1)\rceil$; ordinary $I$ uses $\lceil\tau W\rceil$. Both use the same completed pool and fixed refit schedule and reanchor at the issue floor $|N_t|$. QR selects $\lambda\in\{0.001,0.01,0.1,1,10,\infty\}$ by mean projected-peak pinball loss over the full validation segment. Exact ties choose the greatest shrinkage. The infinity candidate is I and bypasses the finite solver. Every required candidate must complete; a failed candidate cannot be replaced by a different penalty or I. Selection is frozen for evaluation, while coefficients continue to refit. The implementation reuses \texttt{conditional\_study.conditional\_forecast}, \texttt{parsimonious\_v3.forecast} and \texttt{empirical\_headroom.predict}, with their original feature scaling, positive response scale, floor projection, pinball objective and numerical acceptance rules.

At each evaluation origin, the oracle simulates 2000 independent future paths from the known $(N_t,v_t,u_t)$ and future clock. It first updates $v_{t+1}=\omega+\alpha u_t^2+\beta v_t$ and reports the inverted-empirical-CDF quantile of $\max\{|N_t|,\ldots,|N_{t+H}|\}$. This includes the current floor. The finite-path estimate approximates a conditional quantile; its realized loss need not beat F in every repetition. Oracle reports do not depend on W or p, while oracle/F percentages can change with the F denominator.

The formal plan retained 100 repetitions and 500 evaluation origins per repetition. Common random numbers hold paths and origins fixed within a law/repetition; repetitions use separate seed keys. The base entropy is $20261024$, with key $[\mathrm{base},\mathrm{phase},\mathrm{law},\mathrm{rep},\mathrm{stream}]$. Repetition and law indices are zero-based. Pilot/formal phase codes are 1/2; path/oracle stream codes are 0/1. The 2 pilot repetitions served timing only and are excluded from these tables. The frozen run plan used 4 workers, one numerical-library thread each, and a 5400-second hard stop. Optional secondary grids were not executed.

Any required fit, candidate or oracle failure makes the whole factorial cell FAILED. There is no retry, looser tolerance, dropped origin or replacement draw. Later work on that cell is marked \texttt{NOT\_RUN\_CELL\_FAILED}. Completed partial repetitions remain diagnostics and cannot provide a complete-cell median, IQR, win frequency or breach summary. Other cells continue. A calibration failure would fail its law; unfinished deadline work would remain incomplete.

\subsection{Complete main-grid results}\label{sup:v8-mc-results}

The terminal inventory has 17 complete and 7 failed cells. Tables~\ref{tab:v8-mc-loss}--\ref{tab:v8-mc-breaches} retain every planned cell. Negative loss changes favor the column method against F. Median and quartiles are across repetitions of $100(L_A/L_F-1)$. Win is the fraction with $L_{QR}<L_F$; it is not a significance level. The I/F diagnostic uses extra decimals to expose the ordinary-versus-corrected rank difference. No statistic is reported from a failed cell's surviving subset.

\subsection{Interpretation and limits}\label{sup:v8-mc-limits}

These stationary weekly laws permit substantial conditional gains with longer completed history. They therefore do not reproduce the persistent weekly losses in the financial record. D0 is a constant-variance control, not a no-information null: mean reversion changes the conditional position path and its chance of exceeding the current absolute floor. Changing W also changes F's pool and corrected rank, so a QR/F curve compares complete procedures rather than isolating the effect of estimation sample size on QR alone.

Across laws, frequency is bundled with fitted coefficients, volatility and innovation laws, calendar shape, validation length, refit schedule and the physical duration of the forecast horizon. Their separate effects are not identified. Within a law, changing the predictor set also permits a different selected penalty. Infinity selections and the I/F column distinguish ordinary-rank changes from fitted-slope gains descriptively; neither a finite selected penalty nor a lower score alone proves stable conditional information or breach control.

IQRs measure repetition dispersion under fixed estimated parameters; they are not confidence intervals for a median or for real-data performance. The oracle is a finite simulation approximation with known parameters and latent state. Calibration uncertainty, structural breaks, other innovation families and additional dealers are outside this experiment. The saved latent GARCH fourth-moment diagnostic is false for D1 and true for D2, despite finite innovation variances; no normal-limit or finite-fourth-moment argument is used. These simulations neither confirm that the assumed laws are true nor independently validate either financial archive. The unavailable hourly comparisons remain a numerical limitation, not a favorable partial result.

The frozen design, run plan, calibration, every repetition status/candidate record, all summaries and failure contexts are archived under \texttt{protocol/v8/} and \texttt{results/v8/mc/}. The generated fragment's field ledger is \texttt{notes/v8/mc-supplement-bindings.json}.
